title: Thirty Years' War
summary: The Thirty Years' War began in May 1618 with the Bohemian Revolt after the Second Defenestration of Prague. Driven by religious division within the Holy Roman Empire, it drew in Denmark, Sweden and France. Battle, famine and disease killed approximately 8 million people. It ended on 24 October 1648 with the Peace of Westphalia, which the Library of Congress credits with bringing about a sovereignty-based international system.

uncertainty.note: Began with the Second Defenestration of Prague on 23 May 1618; formally concluded with the Peace of Westphalia signed 24 October 1648.

as_recorded.value: The war began in 1618 when the Catholic Emperor, Ferdinand II , tried to enforce religious uniformity on the Empire.

The Thirty Years’ War (1618-1648) was the last major European conflict informed by religious divisions and one of the most devastating in European history resulting in a death toll of approximately 8 million.
On October 24, 1648, the Peace of Westphalia formally ended the Thirty Years War in Europe.

where.historical_name: Prague, Kingdom of Bohemia, Holy Roman Empire

importance.justification: One of the most destructive wars in European history, ending in a peace linked to the modern system of sovereign states.

reviewer_note: The death toll is an estimate from one source. The pin is Prague, where the war began, as a proxy.
